question: In which ways can the flight crew run the cabin pressurisation system?

options.text: Automatically only, with no manual back-up
Manually only, with an automatic safety valve
Automatically, semi-automatically (manual landing elevation) or manually
Automatically or through the emergency ram air only

explanation: Normal operation is fully automatic. Setting LDG ELEV by hand is the semi-automatic case; MODE SEL MAN is full manual control.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: On the ground after landing, how long after touchdown does the outflow valve go fully open?

options.text: Only when the first door is opened

explanation: On the ground before take-off and 55 s after landing the outflow valve opens fully so no residual pressure remains.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: At touchdown, at what cabin vertical speed is any remaining cabin pressure released?
explanation: The residual differential is let out at a controlled 500 ft/min so the ears of the passengers are not hit by a sudden change.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: During take-off, at what rate does the system pre-pressurise the cabin?
explanation: Pre-pressurisation runs at 400 ft/min (cabin descending) to avoid a pressure surge at rotation.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: Pre-pressurisation continues until the differential pressure reaches what value?
explanation: A small positive differential of 0.1 psi is enough to stop the pressure bump when the aircraft rotates.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: Why does the system pre-pressurise the cabin for take-off?

options.text: To cool the avionics before take-off
To check the doors are sealed
To avoid a pressure surge at rotation

explanation: Without a small positive differential the cabin would see a pressure bump as the aircraft rotates.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: When does the pressure controller begin its climb phase?
explanation: The climb phase starts at lift-off, following on from pre-pressurisation.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: In the climb, how does the cabin altitude change?

options.text: At a fixed 1 000 ft/min whatever the aircraft does
It stays at the take-off altitude until cruise
According to a pre-programmed law that takes the aircraft's actual rate of climb into account
It follows the crew's MAN V/S CTL inputs

explanation: The cabin climbs on a schedule that adapts to how fast the aircraft is actually climbing.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: What cabin altitude does the system hold in cruise?

options.text: The level-off value or the landing field elevation, whichever is higher

explanation: If the destination is higher than the cruise cabin altitude, the system holds the destination elevation instead.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: What does the controller aim for during the descent?

options.text: Cabin altitude equal to sea level at touchdown
Cabin pressure equal to the landing field pressure just before landing
Cabin altitude 1 000 ft below the field

explanation: Matching field pressure at touchdown means nothing is left to release when the doors open.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: What is the maximum cabin rate of descent in automatic control?
explanation: The descent rate is limited to 750 ft/min for passenger comfort.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: During a rejected take-off, what does the pressurisation system do?

options.text: It stops the cabin altitude climbing and sets cabin pressure back to take-off altitude + 0.1 psi
It opens the outflow valve fully at once

explanation: The abort phase holds the cabin at the pre-pressurised take-off condition instead of starting a climb.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: With LDG ELEV in AUTO, where does the landing elevation come from?

options.text: From the FMGS, which is used to build an optimised pressure schedule
From the ADIRS barometric setting only

explanation: In AUTO the destination data in the FMGS drive the schedule.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: What range of landing elevation can the crew select with the LDG ELEV selector?
explanation: Any position other than AUTO uses the selected value as the landing elevation reference.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: How should the crew set an accurate manual landing elevation with the LDG ELEV selector?

options.text: By the marks on the selector scale
By reading the value on the ECAM, because the selector scale is only indicative
By entering it in the MCDU
By reading it on the PFD

explanation: The knob's scale is approximate; the ECAM PRESS page shows the value actually selected.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: How does the MODE SEL pushbutton show that manual mode is selected?

options.text: MAN appears in amber with an ECAM caution
A green MAN light on the glareshield
MAN appears in white, and FAULT does not come on

explanation: MAN is a crew choice, so it is white. Amber FAULT is reserved for the failure of both automatic systems.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: When does the MODE SEL FAULT light come on?

options.text: When one automatic system is faulty
When the outflow valve is fully open
When both automatic pressure control systems are faulty

explanation: One failed system is covered by the other. FAULT with an ECAM caution means both are lost and manual control is needed.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: With MODE SEL in MAN, what does holding the MAN V/S CTL switch UP do?

options.text: Moves the outflow valve towards open
Moves the outflow valve towards closed

explanation: UP opens the valve, so the cabin altitude rises. DN closes it.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: With MODE SEL in MAN, what does holding the MAN V/S CTL switch DN do?

options.text: Moves the outflow valve towards open
Moves the outflow valve towards closed

explanation: DN closes the valve, so cabin pressure rises and cabin altitude comes down.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: Why must the MAN V/S CTL switch be held rather than flicked?

options.text: The switch springs back to AUTO if released
The outflow valve moves slowly, so the switch is held until the target vertical speed is reached
A short flick is ignored by the controller
Holding it inhibits the cabin altitude warning

explanation: The valve travel is slow; short inputs barely move it.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: Which of these is NOT closed by the DITCHING pushbutton?

options.text: The avionics ventilation inlet and extract valves

explanation: Ditching closes the openings to the outside: outflow valve, emergency ram air inlet, avionics ventilation inlet and extract valves, and pack flow control valves.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: On the PRESS page, when are the LDG ELEV mode and value hidden?

options.text: When LDG ELEV is in AUTO
When MODE SEL is in MAN

explanation: In manual mode the controller is not using a landing elevation, so it is not displayed.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: Above what cabin vertical speed does the V/S turn amber on the PRESS page?
explanation: Amber above 2 000 ft/min. It begins pulsing green above 1 800 ft/min.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: Above what cabin vertical speed does the V/S indication start pulsing?
explanation: Pulsing is an advisory before the 2 000 ft/min amber limit.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: Above what differential pressure does ΔP turn amber on the PRESS page?
explanation: ΔP turns amber above 8.5 psi (and also when it goes slightly negative).
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: Above what cabin altitude is the cabin altitude shown in red on the PRESS page?
explanation: Red above 9 550 ft corresponds to the cabin altitude warning.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: From what cabin altitude does the cabin altitude indication pulse?
explanation: Pulsing from 8 800 ft gives warning before the 9 550 ft red limit.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: On the PRESS page, what does SYS 1 shown in amber mean?

options.text: System 1 is the active system and it is faulty

explanation: The active system is shown in green normally and in amber when it is faulty.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: What does a green MAN on the PRESS page system indication show?

options.text: The outflow valve is fully open

explanation: With manual mode selected the system indication reads MAN.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: When is SAFETY shown in amber on the PRESS page?

options.text: When the safety valves are fully closed
When the outflow valve is open
When a safety valve is not fully closed
When MODE SEL is in MAN

explanation: Normally the safety valves are closed and SAFETY is white. An open safety valve is abnormal.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: When is the outflow valve diagram shown in amber in flight?

options.text: When it is closed more than 95 %
When the valve is open more than 95 %
Whenever MODE SEL is in MAN

explanation: In flight a nearly fully open outflow valve means the cabin cannot hold pressure.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.
